Question 2 (Power Analysis)
Imagine I want to run a study comparing the spatial recognition memory of currently depressed patients and non-depressed controls in a new, never-before-used way. I found a meta-analysis (Rock et al., 2014) that estimated this difference (using traditional methods) to be d=–0.41. Use {WebPower} to determine how many participants I should recruit in each group in order to have 80% power to detect an effect of this size with α=.05.

title: Week 16 Assignment

In a recent study, my colleagues and I were able to explain 14.3% of the variance in participants’ work performance using 12 low-cost predictors. If we wanted to design a follow-up study to replicate this finding, how many participants would I need to recruit to have 80% omnibus power to detect this same effect (with α=.05)?
(Hint: Be careful not to confuse R² and f²; you will have to do some conversion.)

Read in the screentime dataset (from Canvas) and use it to answer the following questions. Project Description
For this project, you will put the Unit C skills to use. Whereas the assignments in this course use curated datasets that are pre-cleaned and ready-to-analyze, data in the real world is often a bit messy and needs to be tidied. Projects are opportunities to work with real-world data that you care about (e.g., data from your own research lab or domains you care about).
The goal of the Unit C Project is to use a linear model to analyze data you care about and interpret the results. This data could be the same as or different from the data you prepared in the Unit A Project. You should create a Quarto document that conducts these steps, prints the output, and describes your findings in text.

Your dataset

At least 20 rows and at least 4 columns
Some datasets include hundreds of columns and that can be overwhelming, so I recommend selecting a subset of the most important/interesting columns to focus on for this project
Ideally there would be a mix of categorical and continuous variables (but this is not required)



Your focal model
Fit one focal multiple regression model that includes:

An outcome variable and at least two predictors
At least one interaction between two of your predictors

Before you fit it, state in text what you expect and why — name the hypotheses your model is testing, in your own words, rather than only reporting what came out.


What to report

State your hypotheses before fitting the model.
Estimate the focal model and present the coefficient table.
Interpret every coefficient in text, including the intercept. For the interaction, say what it means in terms of your variables — not just whether it was significant.
Probe the interaction. Report simple slopes (for a continuous moderator) or marginal contrasts (for a categorical one), and explain what they show.
Report effect sizes: standardized slopes and \(R^2\).
Include a marginal effects plot of the interaction, and use it to support your interpretation in text.
Check the assumptions of your focal model — correct functional form, no perfect collinearity, constant error variance, normal residuals, independent residuals, and influential cases/outliers. Say what you checked, what you found, and whether it changes your confidence in the results.



Grading







1 point
Was the focal model specified and estimated properly, including the interaction?
